title: Analytics Script Performance Benchmarks (2026)
description: Recorded transfer size, decoded weight, and Slow 4G page-load overhead for Fathom, Plausible, Umami, DataFast, PostHog, and GA4 — measured on AnalyticsVS controlled fixtures, never estimated.
quickAnswer: **Seven recorded AnalyticsVS benchmarks** put Fathom, Plausible, Umami, and DataFast in a light cluster (~**2.7–6.4 KiB** transfer, about **+230–260 ms** Slow 4G load overhead) and GA4 / PostHog in a heavy cluster (~**144–171 KiB** transfer, about **+1.2–1.3 s** overhead). Decoded size is what the browser parses — and it is much larger than the download. Full run reports stay on AnalyticsVS; we never publish estimated script weights.

sections.title: Why analytics script weight matters
sections.content:
Most performance work focuses on *your* code: images, fonts, framework bundles. The analytics tag often gets a free pass because it feels like "just tracking."

It still competes for bandwidth and main-thread time on every page view. On a marketing site that only needs pageviews and goals, a lightweight tag is usually enough. On a product analytics stack that ships session replay, feature flags, and a full SDK, you are buying capability — and paying for it in kilobytes and milliseconds.

This Learn post packages our **recorded** script benchmarks into one matrix so you can compare tools before you dig into individual run reports.

sections.title: How AnalyticsVS measures (and what we skip)
sections.content:
Every number in the matrix comes from our **minimal-v1** fixture — a static HTML page with the vendor's default snippet, no fonts, images, frameworks, GTM, or consent managers. We run **seven cold navigations** per tool plus a paired blank baseline on **simulated Slow 4G** in Chromium.

Published load times show the **added** cost of the tag (with-analytics minus baseline), not a marketing claim about "tiny scripts."

**What v1 measures:** transfer size, decoded body size, script load time, page-load overhead, and whether the install is render-blocking.

**What v1 does not claim yet:** heap allocation, Lighthouse score deltas, field LCP/INP/CLS, or multi-tag GTM containers. If another site publishes those columns from a single DevTools pass, treat them as a different methodology — useful context, not interchangeable with our averages.

Full procedure: [benchmark methodology](/methodology/).

sections.title: Transfer size vs decoded size
sections.content:
Transfer size is what travels over the wire after compression. Decoded size is what the browser parses and executes. Those numbers diverge — sometimes by a lot.

On our recorded runs, Plausible transfers about **3.2 KiB** and decodes to about **5.9 KiB**. GA4 transfers about **170.5 KiB** and decodes to about **507.6 KiB**. PostHog sits in the same heavy band on transfer and decoded weight because the default web snippet pulls a full product SDK, not a pageview-only beacon.

If you only compare gzipped marketing numbers, you understate the parse and compile work the device still has to do.

sections.title: How to read load overhead
sections.content:
On an empty test page, lightweight tools (Fathom, Plausible, Umami, DataFast default and cookieless) cluster around **+230–260 ms** of page-load overhead under Slow 4G. GA4 lands around **+1.16 s**. PostHog lands around **+1.29 s**.

On a real site those milliseconds do not stack additively on top of every other asset — downloads overlap. Still, the empty-page overhead is a clean lower bound for "how expensive is this tag in isolation?"

Every install we have recorded so far is **async or defer** and **non-blocking**. Script *weight* and *initialization work* are the differentiators, not classic parser-blocking snippets.

sections.title: Choosing a tool with performance in mind
sections.content:
**If you need simple web analytics** (pages, referrers, goals) and care about script weight: start with [Fathom](/tools/fathom/), [Plausible](/tools/plausible/), [Umami](/tools/umami/), or [DataFast](/tools/datafast/) — then compare features and price, not only bytes.

**If you need product analytics, flags, or replay:** [PostHog](/tools/posthog/) is a different category. Expect a heavier script; decide whether that capability is worth the cost on marketing pages vs app routes.

**If you need Google Ads / GA4 ecosystem depth:** [Google Analytics 4](/tools/google-analytics-4/) remains the default — with a heavier footprint and more compliance work.

Next step: open the head-to-head pages for your shortlist, then run your traffic through the [pricing calculator](/calculators/pricing/).

sections.title: What we are measuring next
sections.content:
This matrix only includes tools with **recorded** AnalyticsVS benchmarks. Matomo and additional install variants are still on the backlog. When those runs publish, this page updates — we do not fill gaps with estimates.

For per-run charts, environment notes, and raw ranges, open each linked benchmark report from the matrix above.
